chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man from the people of Al-Madinah, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is placed upon the Scale of a person on the Day of Judgement, nothing is superior to good manners.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed placed on the Scale on the Day of Judgement?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni places this hadith in the chapter on good manners, underscoring the Shia emphasis on akhlaq as the practical manifestation of faith. The Prophet’s statement that nothing outweighs good character on the Scale (Mizan) highlights its role as the ultimate criterion for divine acceptance, linking inner piety with outward social conduct. This concept is central to Shia ethics, where moral excellence is seen as the culmination of spiritual refinement.

en.hubeali:
Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from a man from the people of Al Medina, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘No matter would be Placed upon the Scale on the Day of Judgement which is more superior than the good manners’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from a man from the people of Madina from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “On the Day of Judgment, in the balance of a man, no other things will be as meritorious as excellence in moral behavior.”’”
